name: Fata
body:
Fata
CR 20/MR 8

A beautiful, matronal woman in a long dress greets you with an enigmatic smile. Her eyes glitter with the same light as the golden wand in her hands.

XP 307,200
CG Medium fey (mythic)
Init +6; Senses low-light vision, detect desires, detect chaos/evil/good/law; Perception +37

DEFENSE

AC 36, touch 20, flat-footed 30 (+4 Deflection, +6 Dex, +16 natural)
hp 295 (26d6+156+48)
Fort +4, Ref +8, Will +5
DR 20/cold iron and epic; Immune charm and compulsion effects, curse effects, sleep; Resist acid 30, cold 30, electricity 30, fire 30; SR 39

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.; air walk, granted stride, water walk
Melee wand (+4 conductive light mace) +23/+18/+13 (1d6+10)
Special Attacks mythic power 19/day, surge +1d10, vengeful curse, witch hexes (ameliorating, charm, disguise, healing, major ameliorating, major healing, minor prophecy, prophecy, vision, Weather Control, witch’s charge; DC 27)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 20th; concentration +28)

Constant—air walk, detect desires, detect chaos/evil/good/law, water walk
At will—animal messenger, assumed likeness (DC 19), ghost sound (DC 18), mage hand, hex ward
7/day—bestow curse (DC 21), bear’s endurance, bull’s strength, cat’s grace, eagle’s splendor, fox’s cunning, owl’s wisdom
3/day—contact other plane, greater hex glyph (DC 23), greater status, heroes’ feast, mirage arcana (DC 23), plane shift, symbol of sleep (DC 23)
1/day—freedom, greater bestow curse (DC 26), overwhelming presence (DC 27), polymorph any object (DC 26), true prognostication, wish (DC 27)
1/week—binding (DC 26), resplendent mansion, temporal stasis (DC 26)

Witch Spells Known (CL 20th; concentration +28)

9th (6/day)—heroic invocation, mage’s disjunctionp (DC 27), mass hold monster (DC 31), refuge
8th (7/day)—demand (DC 30), mass charm monster (DC 30), maze, protection from spellsP
7th (7/day)—heal, mass hold person (DC 29), spell turningP , vision
6th (7/day)—animate objects, geas/quest (DC 28), globe of invulnerabilityP, guards and wards (DC 24)
5th (7/day)—baleful polymorph (DC 27), break enchantment, dreamp, major creation, mass charm person (DC 27)
4th (8/day)—complex hallucination (DC 22), conditional curse (DC 22), lesser geas (DC 26), lesser globe of invulnerabilityP, minor creation
3rd (8/day)—anthropomorphic animal (DC 25), conjure carriage, dispel magic, magic vestment, remove curse
2nd (8/day)—apport object, bestow insight, conditional favor, enthrall (DC 24), hold person (DC 24), owl’s wisdom
1st (8/day)—beguiling gift (DC 23), charm person (DC 23), command (DC 23), hex vulnerability (DC 19), shield of faith, sleep (DC 23)
0th (at will)—arcane mark, dancing lights, daze (DC 22), detect magic, guidance, mending, message, read magic, resistance

Patron Wisdom

STATISTICS

Str 10, Dex 23, Con 20, Int 24, Wis 27, Cha 26
Base Atk +13; CMB +19; CMD 29
Feats Accursed Hex, Agile Maneuvers, Conditional Spell, Enlarge Spell, Eschew Materials, Extend Spell, Great Fortitude, Greater Spell Focus (Enchantment), Greater Spell Focus (transmutation), Improved Counterspell, Mythic PatronMF, Spell Focus (Enchantment), Spell Focus (transmutation), Weapon Finesse
Skills Craft (alchemy, another one) +36, Diplomacy +37, Knowledge (arcana, history, nobility, planes) +33, Knowledge (nature) +36, Perception +37, Perform (any one) +37, Sense Motive +37, Spellcraft +36, Use Magic Device +37
Languages Abyssal, Celestial, Common, Elven, Gnome, Infernal, Sylvan, Treant; speak with animals, speak with plants
SQ a thousand faces, call protégé, change shape (any animal or plant; greater polymorph), countercurseM, crafting mastery, godmother’s blessing, mythic spellcasting, mythic spell-like abilities, sanctum

SPECIAL ABILITIES

A Thousand Faces (Su)

A fata can change her appearance at will as with alter self, like a druid.

Countercurse (Su)

A fata can counter curse spells using another spell of any level with the same descriptor. A countercurse grants to the fata a +20 bonus on Spellcraft checks made to counterspell. If the counterspell is successful, the target of the countered curse is affected by the fata’s countercurse instead. This ability is most often used to replace a more powerful curse with a milder, easier to dispel effect. A fata can use countercurse in conjunction with vengeful curse.

Godmother’s Blessing (Su)

A fata can grant great boons to a mortal she protects. By expending one use of mythic power, a fata can bestow a blessing to another creature she designed as her ward, choosing among the following effects:

+12 bonus to an ability score, or +6 bonus to two ability scores (to a maximum ability score of 30).
+8 bonus on attack rolls, saves, ability checks, or skill checks.
The ward can use a 1st- or 2nd- level spell as a spell-like ability once per day.
Permanent greater age resistance and youthful appearance.

The fata can also invent her own blessing, that should be no more powerful than those described above. The effect of a godmother’s blessing is permanent; however, a fata can decide to apply a condition to her blessing, as per conditional favor . If the ward violates this condition, the boon is lost and the ward must succeed at a Will saving throw or be afflicted by bestow curse. Otherwise, only wish, miracle or equivalent spell can cancel a godmother’s blessing. However, anyone who attempts to remove the blessing (whether successful or not) other than by the means stipulated by the fata when first bestowing it must succeed at a Will saving throw or be afflicted by greater bestow curse. This ability can be used in conjunction with vengeful curse.

Spellcasting

A fata casts spells as a 20th-level sorcerer but selects her spells from the witch’s spell list. Many fata can also have researched spells from other classes’ lists. In addition, each fata selects a specific witch patron and adds that patron’s granted spells to her list of spells known.

Vengeful Curse (Su)

When a fata casts a curse, either as a spell or a spell-like ability, she can state a condition under which the curse is broken, ending its effect. This functions as conditional curse, except there are no time or wording limits to the condition and the fata can apply a condition to a normal, major, or greater curse.

The fata can expend mythic power to make this ability work as mythic conditional curse.

Wand (Ex)

Each fata has a special bond with her magic wand. The wand has the abilities of a rod of splendor (except the fata can also create a noble garb on another creature touching it with the wand) and can be wielded as a +4 conductive light mace; it also acts as a witch’s familiar and stores the fata’s spells. As long as the fata holds her wand, she gains a +4 deflection bonus on her AC. At will, she can use the wand to cast magic circle against chaos, evil, good, or law, centered on herself. In the hands of anyone other than its owner, the wand is just a rod of splendor. A fata deprived of her wand cannot cast witch spells or use witch hexes.

Witch Hexes

A fata can use hexes as a 20th-level witch.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary or court (1-7)
Treasure double (magic wand, other treasure)

Fata are among the mightiest fey, and most often than not, also their sovereigns. Some legends speak of them as of the original spellcasters, who set the rules for magic and taught the first spells to mortals; others see them as ex-celestials exiled from the Upper Planes, or lesser deities charged with watching over the elements of the world and the destinies of mortals (as their name implies). Folk tales speak of fata as the good counterpart to hags; actually, it is said that all evil fata eventually are transformed into hags. This would explain why very few evil fata do exist. Fata are always female, without exceptions.

Fata tend to live in their own guarded lands and private demiplanes, connected both with the Material Plane and the First World, where they build secluded castles and hold court, surrounded by other fata, lesser fey at their service or, sometimes, living alone (neutral and evil fata in particular tend to isolate themselves from the outer world and loathe visitors). As guardians of destiny, they can devise trials for heroes that manage to find their abodes, dispense wisdom and knowledge of the future, or give warnings and punishments to kings and princes who stray from the right path. Other fata are known to bestow magical arms and armor, magical mounts, or other powerful items to destined mortals; some of them ward time-forgotten artifacts, waiting for the champion who will claim them.

Though mostly benevolent, fata are notoriously fickle and capricious. Offending one of them can lead to having your whole family cursed for generations. On the other hand, someone being properly respectful towards these most potent of fey may gain their protection not only for themselves, but for their children and descendants. A fata who accepts to be the godmother of a mortal child will watch upon her ward for their entire life and assist them in their distress (though she might not be allowed to spare them that distress). While fata can’t directly interfere with the destiny of mortals, they know the critical joints when destiny can be subtly influenced and exploit this knowledge, often in their own mysterious ways.

A fata can sometimes fall in love with a worthy mortal; the child of such a union may inherit great magic potential but doesn’t become a fata save in exceptional circumstances.
